headline: PACMAN paper reports a real-time AI control framework deployed in DIII-D experiments
summary: A November 2025 author preprint, later identified in a July 2026 journal record, describes PACMAN, a real-time software framework integrating plasma diagnostics, model/controller components and actuator commands in the DIII-D tokamak control system. Its authors report five experimental applications, including reinforcement-learning control, event prediction and profile control. The manuscript gives device-specific architecture and timing details, but the deployment is CPU-based and limited to DIII-D; the paper frames extension to other devices as prospective. These are author-reported demonstrations, with no independent reproduction or matched comparative performance analysis in this review.
